mask_guide.title: Respirator guide for particle pollution
mask_guide.subtitle: Fit, limits, and local certification matter when choosing a particulate respirator.
mask_guide.which_mask_desc: A properly fitting particulate respirator certified by a recognized authority can reduce exposure to particles. Choose one that fits closely and follow its instructions; masks and respirators differ by model and certification.
fit_tips: Choose a genuine particulate respirator certified by the authority in your country.
Follow the manufacturer instructions for putting it on and positioning the nosepiece and straps.
Check the fit each time using the instructions supplied with the respirator; gaps let unfiltered air in.
Facial hair or anything else crossing the sealing surface can interfere with the seal.
mask_guide.limits_desc: Particulate respirators filter particles, not gases, and do not supply oxygen. Wearing one can make breathing harder. People with heart or lung conditions should seek advice from a healthcare professional. Reduce outdoor exposure and follow local public-health guidance.
mask_guide.pediatric_desc: Fit and suitability depend on the child, product, and local guidance. A poorly fitting or uncomfortable respirator may not be worn correctly. Check current advice for children; do not assume an adult size will fit.

glossary.title: Air Quality & Inversion Glossary
glossary.subtitle: Plain explanations of environmental and air purification science
glossary.aqi_desc: The US AQI is a 0–500 index. Its categories are Good (0–50), Moderate (51–100), Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups (101–150), Unhealthy (151–200), Very Unhealthy (201–300), and Hazardous (301+).
glossary.pm25_desc: Fine particles with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 micrometers or less. They can be inhaled into the respiratory system; health effects depend on exposure and individual factors.
glossary.inversion_desc: A winter weather condition where a layer of warm air sits above cold ground air, trapping smoke, exhaust, and dust like a giant lid.
glossary.convective_mixing_desc: Sunlight can heat the ground and promote vertical mixing, but pollution varies by day and place. An hourly forecast may show relative changes; it cannot identify a guaranteed safe time or a street-level condition.
glossary.cadr_desc: The volume of filtered, clean air an air purifier delivers per hour, measured in cubic meters per hour (m³/h). Higher CADR cleans a room faster.
glossary.corsi_desc: A do-it-yourself air cleaner concept using a box fan and particle filters. Performance, safety, sound, and cost depend on the exact fan, filters, build, room, and local prices. Follow current safety guidance.

footer.safety_text: Aura is designed for exposure avoidance and environmental harm reduction. It is not a clinical diagnostic system. If you or a family member experiences severe breathlessness, chest tightness, or blue lips, seek emergency medical care immediately.
footer.emergency_call: For emergencies, contact your local emergency service.
footer.built_with: Built for urban clean air equity and scientific transparency.
